location: Results (Effect of L-DOPA administration post extinction on extinction memory retrieval, p. 4) and Discussion
quote: We could not replicate the facilitating effect of L-DOPA on extinction retrieval (hypothesis 1) and on the number of vmPFC reactivations (hypothesis 3).
reason: For the target preregistered test of hypothesis 1 on p. 4 (the relationship between post-extinction L-DOPA administration and extinction memory retrieval at test), the authors explicitly report that they did not confirm an effect of L-DOPA (F(1,53) = 0.02, p = 0.887, BF01 = 3.85) and state in the Discussion that they could not replicate hypothesis 1. The shipped value ('mixed') conflates this failed target hypothesis with the replication of hypothesis 2 or non-preregistered exploratory moderation analyses involving salivary alpha-amylase.

location: Abstract, Results (Effect of L-DOPA administration post extinction on vmPFC reactivations, p. 5), and Discussion
quote: In contrast to our previous study, we find no evidence that L-DOPA administration significantly enhances retrieval and that this is mediated by enhancement of the number of vmPFC reactivations.
reason: For the target effect on p. 5 examining the effect of L-DOPA on the number of post-extinction vmPFC reactivations as a mediator of extinction retrieval (hypothesis 3), the authors explicitly state that there was no statistically significant effect of L-DOPA on vmPFC reactivations (F(1,44) = 0.87, p = 0.356, BF01 = 15.00) and conclude in both the Abstract and Discussion that they failed to replicate this effect and its mediation.
